open_points.subject: disclosure-class ordering
open_points.text: “the disclosure classes ... are enumerations of `models`, each ordered by its declared order ... the members and the order have that one home” contradicts `canonical_values` owning “The order of disclosure classes and the highest class of a set”
open_points.question: Does `models` own the disclosure-class order while `canonical_values` only applies it, or does `canonical_values` own the order?
options: `models` owns the enumeration and order; `canonical_values` consumes it to compute the highest class
`canonical_values` owns the disclosure order and `models` only declares the members
open_points.default_guess: `models` owns the enumeration and order; `canonical_values` compares the declared enum positions.

open_points.subject: equal content-record submission
open_points.text: `canonical_values` owns “A01 rules 1 and 4,” although rule 4 says an existing identity returns the existing record unchanged and records nothing, while `canonical_values` “Must not own Where a value is stored”
open_points.question: Which module owns detecting an existing content identity, preserving its first author and store position, and deciding the submission-specific consequences such as rerunning admission?
options: `store` atomically detects and returns existing records, while each domain module owns the operation-specific consequences
Each owning domain module performs the existence check and consequences through generic store reads and writes
`canonical_values` owns the whole equal-submission rule despite not owning persistence
open_points.default_guess: `store` owns atomic insert-if-absent and retrieval of the existing record; `functions`, `flows`, and the other record-producing modules own their operation-specific consequences.

open_points.subject: randomly minted record identities
open_points.text: A01 says `trial_execution_id`, `binding_id`, `run_id`, `approval_id` and `grant_id` “are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is minted again,” but no State 3 module owns random identifier generation or collision retry
open_points.question: Which module generates random identities and guarantees the retry-on-collision rule?
options: `store` mints and collision-checks every random record identity inside the creating transaction
Each record-owning module mints its own identity and asks `store` to reject collisions
A separate lower-level identity capability owns random generation, with `store` checking uniqueness
open_points.default_guess: `store` mints and collision-checks the identity inside the transaction that creates the record.

open_points.subject: captured trial case contract provenance
open_points.text: “`functions.add_captured_trial_case`, which checks that the record's pinned contract version is the one named” requires `functions` to know a `NodeExecution` owned by `runs`, even though `functions` may know only earlier modules; M23 also names only the executed implementation, not a contract version
open_points.question: Which module verifies that the captured NodeExecution's implementation belongs to the named contract version, and what admissible fact is passed across the dependency boundary?
options: `runs` resolves the executed implementation through `functions` and owns the provenance check before calling `add_captured_trial_case`
`runs` passes the executed implementation identity and `functions` verifies that its own implementation belongs to the named contract version
`functions` is allowed a new raw-record or `runs` capability despite the declared dependency direction
open_points.default_guess: `runs` passes the executed implementation identity, and `functions` verifies from its own implementation record that it belongs to the named contract version.
